title: Braking, Skidding & ABS
whatItIs: Brake early and lightly, firmer as you stop. Skids are usually caused by the driver: remove the cause, then steer to recover.
keyFacts: Normal braking: early and light, firmer as you stop, easing off just before the car comes to rest.
Skids usually come from harsh braking, accelerating or steering, or a speed too fast for the conditions.
In a skid, release the brake or ease off the accelerator, and steer into it: rear goes right, steer right.
ABS emergency: brake firmly and hold the pressure until you've slowed. ABS helps you keep steering.
After deep water, test the brakes gently. If weak, apply light pressure while driving slowly to dry them.

onTheTest.question: The rear of your car skids to the left. What should you do?
options: Ease off the cause and steer left
onTheTest.why: Rule 119: remove the cause by releasing the brake or easing off the accelerator, and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

onTheTest.question: On a car test, the wheels lock briefly in the emergency stop, but the candidate regains control. How is this assessed?
onTheTest.why: DT1 section 11 (Controlled stop): locking the wheels and skidding a short distance while regaining control is a driving fault.

traps: ABS doesn't promise a shorter stop: don't assume it.
Applying the handbrake before stopping in the emergency stop is a recorded fault.
Steering unresponsive in the wet? Water may be stopping grip: ease off and slow gradually.
